reva_host: Host or base URL of your Reva tenant, for example `api.example.reva.ai`. Defaults to `api.reva.ai`; a value you set overrides it. Host-only values are called over HTTPS.
auth_token: Bearer token Kong presents to Reva Trust Guardian on every evaluation. Find it in the Reva console under Settings. This field is referenceable — store it in a vault rather than inline.
ssl_verify: Verify the TLS certificate presented by Reva Trust Guardian. Turn this off only against a test instance with a self-signed certificate.
monitor_mode: Evaluate every call and log the verdict, but never block. Use it to see what policy would refuse before you enforce it.
fail_open: Proxy the request when Reva Trust Guardian cannot be reached or returns no decision. Off by default, so an outage refuses calls rather than passing them unevaluated.
deny_status: HTTP status returned when a call is refused, either by policy or because no decision could be obtained.
deny_message: Message returned to the caller in the response body when a call is refused. The specific reason is returned alongside it.
jwt_user_claim: JWT claim read from the bearer token to identify the user. Common values are `sub`, `preferred_username` and `cognito:username`.
jwt_groups_claim: JWT claim holding the user's group memberships, sent to Reva Trust Guardian as groups a policy can match. Use `roles` for RBAC tokens, `realm_access.roles` for Keycloak, or `cognito:groups` for Cognito.
prompt_key: Name of the field that carries the prompt text to Reva. Must match what your policy expects to read.
session_key: Where the thread id is read: an HTTP request header of this name first, then the JSON body. Use dots for a nested body field, such as `params.thread_id`. Nothing else is searched. Sent to Reva Trust Guardian on a turn's first call only.
hop_ttl: How long, in seconds, the policy keeps a turn open when its first call never finishes. Set it longer than your slowest agent turn.
forward_traceparent: Pass the `traceparent` used for the authorization decision on to the upstream service, so one trace id spans the gateway and your backend.
debug: Log each decision and the request sent to Reva Trust Guardian at notice level. Use it while tuning policy; leave it off in production.
